ImageNet-R-50 replay-adaptation diagnosis

A paired test of stage-random replay, equal task weighting, optimizer-state resets, and fresh full-history integration at fragmented frontiers.

Finding. Permuted-MNIST used a fresh deterministic replay draw at every macro-step. The validation-selected online ImageNet-R condition is Rotating replay / example loss / carry Adam. Averaged across matched cells and stages 31/50, rotation changed locked-test accuracy by +1.395 percentage points.

What differed from Permuted-MNIST

Permuted-MNIST sampled uniformly from its complete historical archive with a seed containing the macro-step. It used 256 current and 256 historical examples. ImageNet-R instead used a permanent-priority namespace independent of stage. Stage-keyed random replay remains deterministic and resumable while preserving fixed-H cumulative O(T log T) work.

Interpretation boundaries

The fresh full-history fits use every fit row, three restarts, and validation-loss selection. They are diagnostic ceilings, not online LogT conditions. The integrator validation identities never enter integrator fitting, although the frozen LoRA nodes were previously fitted on all 24,000 training images. This is one seed and a previously examined test split, so test results are descriptive.
